history.summary: The Santoshi Maa Temple at EM/119, Basanti Nagar, Rourkela (Sundargarh district) is a small neighbourhood Hindu shrine; its founding date, builder and management are UNVERIFIED and no web sources describe its history. IDENTITY AMBIGUOUS: several 'Santoshi Maa Temple' listings exist in Rourkela (Basanti Nagar; Uco Bank Colony/Nayabazar Sector 21; others in Bhubaneswar and Semiliguda elsewhere in Odisha) - the CSV row cannot be tied to one with certainty; documented here as the Basanti Nagar shrine, which has a photo listing. Santoshi Mata devotion spread widely across North India after the 1960s-70s, consistent with a modern local shrine. Coordinates are a geocoded full-address match for the Basanti Nagar address. NO reliable image of the actual temple was found after image searching (only map-thumbnails and unrelated results), so media is empty.

town_description: Rourkela is Odisha's second-largest city and its industrial capital, built around the Rourkela Steel Plant set up in the 1950s with German collaboration. It sits on the banks of the Brahmani river in Sundargarh district, near the Ib valley coalfields and the Khandadhar waterfalls. The city is known as the 'Steel City of Odisha' and serves as the main gateway for western Odisha's tribal hinterland.
